title: Network approaches to community detection in nanoscale connectomics
title_zh: 网络科学在纳米级连接组中的社区检测方法
abstract: Although network science has offered insight into the organization and function of nervous systems, much of this work has focused on mesoscale, interareal connectomes. This leaves open the question of whether similar organizational principles apply to nanoscale connectomes, where individual neurons and synapses are the focus. These neuron-level datasets are uniquely complex, necessitating the refinement of existing tools and the development of new ones to handle their distinctive structure. Network science offers a range of approaches for analysing these data. Here, we focus on community detection, a family of methods for identifying subnetworks of functionally related neurons. We suggest that finding such communities could be valuable for several reasons: they could help us understand how modular organization supports adaptability and specialization, serve as a method for dimension reduction, and potentially aid in the discovery of new functional circuits. By reviewing some early applications and discussing contemporary methods, we aim to provide a roadmap for future studies in this emerging field, as we anticipate the arrival of new and more complex datasets. Extracting insight from nanoscale connectomes presents formidable challenges. In this Review, Betzel and colleagues focus on network science applications to these high-dimensional datasets, providing a high-level overview of different community detection methods while discussing which methods suit which questions and the types of biologically meaningful information they can reveal.
